title: ML prior-art search output (one angle)
description: One angle's coverage grid and the ML options it found. The grid is the product: it is what makes an option that does not exist distinguishable from a search that never ran.

cell_status.description: `gated` is this corpus's characteristic failure and is NEW here: a source that answered yesterday and now demands a key is neither unreachable nor forbidden — the fetch completed and was refused. This type lost one channel that way and one to a REDIRECT, which is `superseded` — two losses, two different statuses. `rate-limited` is a normal operating condition for the shared academic pools, never a searched zero. `superseded` is a 301 to a live replacement: the fetch SUCCEEDED, and recording it as unreachable hides that the corpus is moving under the survey.

cell.description: One (group x active source) pair. The owed set is DERIVED — the angle's `applicable_group_types` selects the groups, the angle's own source list selects the sources — so it is never every group against every source.

group_id.description: A group minted in the wave-0 map, verbatim.

source_id.description: A registry source that the map recorded ACTIVE.

queries.description: EVERY query run for this pair, verbatim AS RUN — whatever the channel. Several sources here are APIs, so a query is the request you issued and, where you filtered the response, the expression you filtered with. A paraphrase cannot be re-run, and a coverage record that cannot be re-run proves nothing.

timestamp.description: When this pair was searched. Per cell, not per file: nine angles against a fast-moving corpus can span a day, and a single file-level date hides which half is stale.

returned.description: How many ITEMS the source returned under the frame `count_frame` states. Required when status is `reached`. NULL — never 0 — for any other status: a zero meaning 'we could not look' is the failure this survey exists to prevent.

count_frame.description: What `returned` counted and how, stated so a reader can re-derive it: 'models listed by the API for this pipeline_tag, first page', 'rows in the published results table'. Required whenever `returned` is above 0 — this corpus yields several defensible counts for one page, and a count without its frame is not re-derivable.

kept.description: How many distinct candidate ROWS this cell carried forward into `candidates` PLUS `unadmitted` — the reading market-competitive, visual and user-research all use. NEVER a result count. It must EQUAL the candidates citing this cell plus the `unadmitted` entries whose `found_by` names it; counting only candidates would score a row dropped without a record as correct.

cause.description: Required for every non-`reached` status, with OBSERVABLE evidence: an HTTP status, a redirect target, the error body, the rate-limit header. 'Could not access' is not a cause.

fallback_used.description: The fallback actually walked, prefixed with which level it came from — `angle:<id>` or `row:<id>`. Every registry row names a fallback and every angle names one; they differ, and one bare id cannot say which was taken.

sanitization.description: Per-cell sanitization record, where this cell's fetch differed from the map's wave-0 posture for the same source.

candidate.description: One ML OPTION — a single addressable, adoptable artifact. Not a paper, not a vendor, not a research direction: if it cannot be adopted, it is not a candidate.

item_id.description: The canonical identity, prefixed by its id class. Six of the seven prefixes are governed by someone else's grammar, which is why `id_class` is checked rather than assumed.

id_class.description: Must agree with `item_id`'s prefix. Recorded separately so the check is an equality rather than a parse.

found_by.description: The (group_id, source_id) CELL this option came out of, written `group/source` — the same form and the same meaning the sibling types give it. Its evidence must be about THAT group: an option filed under a group its evidence does not serve collapses two axes into one row. `kept` on that cell counts these rows plus the `unadmitted` ones naming it, so a cell key that does not resolve makes the arithmetic unclosable.

authority.description: WHO stands behind the quoted claim, never who published the artifact. `independent-benchmark`: a third party who evaluated it and has no stake. `peer-reviewed`: a venue that reviewed it before publication. `vendor-published`: the ORGANISATION that produced it. `self-reported`: the INDIVIDUAL who uploaded it, about their own work — a community Hub upload under a personal namespace is this. `community-reported`: someone who is neither the author nor an independent evaluator. `unattributed`: no identifiable author. RANKS, never CUTS — a vendor benchmark is recorded and ordered below an independent one, not excluded, because excluding on authority is how a survey silently becomes an opinion.

locator.description: A resolvable URL. An option with no locator cannot be adopted and is not admitted.

as_of.description: When the FACT became true. NULL when the content states none — never defaulted to the fetch date, which would be a fabricated fact about the world.

source_claimed_modified_at.description: The page's claim about ITSELF. A claim, not a fact: recorded here so it can never be promoted into `as_of` by accident.

source_claim_provenance.description: Where the self-claimed date came from. `absent` is recorded explicitly rather than left null-by-omission.

evidence_quote.description: The load-bearing sentence or field value, VERBATIM from the locator. Not a paraphrase: the conditions judge the claim against this text, and a paraphrase is your reading rather than the document's words.

claim.description: What the DOCUMENT says, in your words — never what the model DOES. `evidence_quote` is the warrant; where the two disagree, the quote governs.

finding.description: An ABSENCE that is itself evidence: 'the card states no evaluation on any held-out split'. Recorded here rather than left as an empty field, because a hole reads as an oversight and this reads as a fact about the corpus.

evaluation.description: REQUIRED on any candidate carrying a leaderboard or benchmark result. A rank is not a quality signal — it is a claim under a stated evaluation, on a stated split, at a stated date. The benchmark and the split are REQUIRED; `measured_on` is null when the table publishes no date, and an undated result is still carried. Dropping it would discard the measured comparison the survey exists to gather.

split.description: The exact split the number is on. 'test' and 'validation' are different numbers, and a leaderboard that does not say which is a leaderboard you cannot compare against.

measured_on.description: When the result was produced. Null when the table states none — which is itself worth knowing.

provenance.description: The paper, DOI and code behind the artifact. A paper is never a record (a paper cannot be adopted); its identifier lives here, on the artifact it introduced.

licence.description: Recorded verbatim as the source states it, including 'unstated'. Not normalised to an SPDX id we chose: the field that decides adoption is the one the vendor actually wrote.

schema_version.description: The version THIS schema validates. A const, not a floor.

note.description: Run-level context that is not a cross-group lead — a throttle observed, a mirror used. `notes` is for leads.

outcome.description: `ran` you searched. `not_run` the map's own verdict for this angle was `holds: false`, so you did NOT search: no cells and no candidates, and searching anyway inflates the survey with an angle the scope ruled out. `vacated` you started and there was nothing to search — every source non-reachable, or every owed pair deliberately not attempted. Cells and causes are owed; candidates are not.

not_run.description: Why, when outcome is `not_run`. Names the map verdict being honoured.

coverage.description: One cell per owed (group x source) pair. A pair in the owed set with no cell is an unexplained gap, not a zero.

retrieval_summary.description: Duplicates the cells DELIBERATELY. A discrepancy between this and the grid is the signal that a failure was laundered into a zero.

bound.description: The per-angle limit, whether it bound, and the ordering it truncated by.

cap.description: The REGISTRY's cap for this angle. A run may neither raise its own ceiling nor quietly lower it.

hit.description: Whether the cap TRUNCATED: true when the ordering had more to give and the cap stopped it, false when it did not. It reports what the run observed and nothing wider — false is NOT a claim that the corpus was exhausted, which no cap over a ~10^5-item registry could support and which this angle's own reference denies.

ordering.description: The rule the truncation selected by, stated so a reader can re-apply it. An outcome restated ('the best models first') cannot be re-applied and so cannot show what was dropped.

dropped_note.description: What fell out, when `hit` is true. Without it the ordering is the ONLY evidence a truncation leaves.

ordering_deviation.description: Set when you did NOT apply the declared ordering, with the reason. A declared ordering a producer may never depart from is a worse rule than one that requires the departure to be recorded.

unadmitted.description: Options found but NOT carried into `candidates`, recorded rather than dropped — a silent drop makes 'we did not look' indistinguishable from 'we looked and rejected it', one layer down.

found_by.description: The CELL that produced it, written `group/source` — identical in form and meaning to a candidate's. Required because `kept` reconciles per cell against candidates PLUS these rows: with a 2-D grid a bare source id names four cells at once and the arithmetic cannot close, which is how a dropped row hides.

reason.description: Why it was not carried. A reason a reader could act on, not a restatement of the outcome.

notes.description: Cross-group leads found while working this angle. The correct channel for something that belongs to another group — never a candidate row.
